name: Harsha
overview: Harsha was a male member of the tribe of Levi who served as a temple servant. His role is specifically noted in the context of the post-exilic community, highlighting his participation in the restoration of temple worship. There are no additional personal notes recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Harsha means 'deaf' in Hebrew. This proper name is recorded without indication that it was given directly by God, simply identifying him in the biblical record.
familyAndRelationships: Harsha is identified as a descendant of Levi, indicating his Levitical heritage. Beyond this tribal affiliation, Scripture does not provide further family relationships for him.
scriptureSignificance: Harsha’s significance lies in his service as a temple servant during the period of Israel's return from exile, as documented in Ezra. His inclusion among the Levites underscores the restoration of temple functions and the continuity of priestly duties in the post-exilic community. Though not a prominent figure, his role reflects the faithful reestablishment of worship in Jerusalem.
